name: Bu Dai
catalog_citation: Kosaka, Ryuichi. 1997. A Phonology of the Bu Dai (Thu Lao) Language. Journal of Asian and African Studies (ILCAA, Tokyo) 53: 137-153.
catalog_quote: The Bu Dai language is fundamentally, as the other Tai dialects, a monosyllabic tonal language, the syllabic structure of which is C1V(C2)/T3) (where the appearance of C2 is not obligatory). C1 is the initial consonant, V is the vocalic nucleus and C2 is the final consonant. T is a supra-segmental feature — the tone. ... [fn. 3] Strictly speaking, there is an occasional so-called 'minor syllable' attached in front of this fundamental word structure. In terms of stress, it is always weaker than that of the following major syllable and its segmental realization varies slightly according to the vowel in the major syllable. Tonally, there seems to be a difference at least between 'high (ˊ)' and 'middle (ˉ)'. Though, it is not yet clear whether or not there are minimal pairs involving this tonal difference in the minor syllable. ... In this article, we focused on major syllables and abstaine…
sweep_summary: Dai Zhuang (daiz1235) is in the catalog as 'tonal' on Kosaka 1997 (Bu Dai/Thu Lao phonology, p.139 + fn.3). The search of works with stress or accent in the title returned a single item, Glottolog 613012 = Kuzla & Ernestus 2007 'Prosodic conditioning of phonetic detail of German plosives' (ICPhS XVI). I downloaded the open MPG PuRe copy with) and read it: it is an acoustic study of German word-initial plosives with no mention of any Tai language; the Glottolog record itself (saved) flags the link as 'computerized assignment from \"plosives\"'. classification: not about Dai Zhuang, silent on the catalog's classification, priority none; the Glottolog attachment should be treated as noise. No new first-hand stress statement was found; the Johnson 2011 SIL survey already held by the project (7467 lines) contains no word-stress statement for Dai Zhuang either (only Li 1977's 'accent on the first vowel' of Proto-Tai diphthongs, line 4525). The catalog's Kosaka 1997 quote was re-read from the saved page image and stands. direct downloads (MPG PuRe, Glottolog) succeeded.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage (p.139 sect. 1.1 + fn.3, p.143 sect. 1.4) is present verbatim in the Kosaka 1997 PDF we hold, read as page images because the scan has no text layer; grade 'page-image' is honest. (2) Deciding source: a 1997 first-hand phonology article, the sole Glottolog descriptive reference for daiz1235 (the other four Glottolog entries are misattached Korean papers). Identity Bu Dai/Thu Lao = zhd confirmed from the ISO 639-3 change request. (3) Alternatives: web search found no prosody/stress or instrumental study of Dai Zhuang or Thu Lao; the largest open description, Johnson 2011 (SIL EWP 2011-005, 170 pp), was downloaded and is silent on stress, treating Dai Zhuang purely as a tone language — consistent with the 'tonal' coding.
